papers.title: Finite time blow-up for the Willmore flow of symmetric figure-eight tori
papers.abstract: We show that the Willmore flow of symmetric figure-eight tori of revolution produces a finite time singularity, provided the initial energy is below $12\pi$. Our approach relies on the connection with elastic curves in the hyperbolic plane and a fine analysis of Palais--Smale sequences in the relevant energy regime.

papers.title: Remarks on uniqueness and nonuniqueness for the isotropic $L_p$-Minkowski problem with $p<-n$
papers.abstract: We study uniqueness and nonuniqueness for the isotropic $L_p$-Minkowski problem with $p<-n$. For $n\geq3$, we prove uniqueness for $p$ just below $-n$ without any symmetry assumptions. Moreover, for $n\geq8$, we obtain nonuniqueness for $p$ just above $-2n-3$, even under full simplex symmetry. The proofs use the Chou-Wang obstruction and Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction.

papers.title: Structured Design of Layered Sparse Unitary Space-Time Modulation for Integrated Noncoherent and Coherent MIMO Communications
papers.abstract: This work presents a novel structured constellation design based on unitary space-time modulation (USTM) for integrated noncoherent and coherent multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications. Information is encoded into the sparse space-time matrices through two layers: a noncoherent layer that distinguishes points on the Grassmann manifold (subspaces) and a coherent layer that distinguishes among the Stiefel representatives associated with each of those points (bases for the subspaces). We consider sequential decoding of the two layers to reduce computational complexity, while explicitly identifying the matrix structures that favor this decoding strategy. The proposed constellation builds on a previous structured Grassmannian signaling design, which has the remarkable property of producing space-time matrices with a single nonzero entry per row, while introducing a novel systematic design for the second layer corresponding to the Stiefel representatives. The design of the second layer preserves the sparsity of the first layer and significantly reduces the decoding computational complexity, while ensuring reliable performance under sequential decoding and enabling a simple yet effective bit labeling, as validated by numerical results in terms of bit error rate (BER) and symbol error rate (SER). Numerical results also show graceful performance degradation under channel correlation and, for limited coherence intervals where channel state information at the receiver (CSIR) can be estimated only imperfectly, improved performance compared with classical space-time block coding (STBC) schemes based on QAM and PSK.

papers.title: Hyperk\"ahler Periods in Families of Parabolic Higgs Bundle Moduli Spaces
papers.abstract: We consider the period map on families of parabolic Higgs bundle moduli spaces with varying parabolic weights $\alpha$ and Higgs field eigenvalues $\sigma$. We assemble the moduli spaces into a smooth family $\pi:\mathscr M\to\Lambda$ where $\Lambda$ encodes $(\alpha,\sigma)$, and define parallel transport for homology along paths in an open dense subset $\Lambda_0\subset\Lambda$. By generalizing a classical theorem of Duistermaat and Heckman, we prove that the period map is affine linear in $(\alpha,\sigma)$, with slope governed by the curvature class of a principal torus bundle over $\mathscr M$. For the four-dimensional moduli spaces of types $E_6,E_7,E_8$, we compute these classes to get explicit formulas for the period maps.

papers.title: Gradient estimates and monotonicity formulae for the $p$-filtration equation on Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We derive Li--Yau type estimates on closed Riemannian manifolds and local Hamilton-type gradient estimates on complete manifolds for the $p$-filtration equation $u_t=\Delta_pF(u)$. Under nonnegative Ricci curvature and a structural condition on $F$, we establish a $\mathcal W$-entropy formula, entropy-power concavity and local entropy rigidity. We also prove a parabolic frequency monotonicity formula without curvature assumptions. The results include homogeneous doubly nonlinear diffusion and extend to nonhomogeneous power sums and the arctangent law.

papers.title: Extremal metrics for the $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalues
papers.abstract: We study the $G$-invariant Steklov spectrum of compact connected Riemannian manifolds with boundary, endowed with an effective isometric action of a compact Lie group $G$. Under a mild nontransitivity assumption on the boundary action, we establish that this spectrum consists of an infinite sequence of eigenvalues diverging to infinity. We then investigate extremal metrics for the normalised $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalue functionals. Assuming that $\dim G \geq 1$, we prove that none of these functionals admits an extremal $G$-invariant metric. Moreover, when $\dim M \geq 3$, the normalised first $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalue is unbounded above even within a fixed $G$-invariant conformal class. The proof relies on a local model near a boundary orbit and spectral convergence under conformal collapse. Finally, in contrast with the upper bounds obtained by Colbois, Dryden and El Soufi for invariant Laplace eigenvalues of embedded spheres of revolution, we construct, for any $n \geq 3$, a sequence of smooth Euclidean domains of revolution in $\mathbb R^n$, all diffeomorphic to the ball, along which the normalised first $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalue blows up.

papers.title: Gradient estimate for $p$-heat equation on complete Riemannian manifold
papers.abstract: We derive a Hamilton-type gradient estimate for positive solutions to the $p$-heat equation via the Moser iteration method. Our result relaxes the curvature assumption from sectional curvature to Ricci curvature. In addition, we obtain a Liouville-type theorem and a Harnack-type inequality as corollaries.

papers.title: The Minimal Background Period for Infinitely Many Spectral Gaps in Anderson-Bernoulli Models
papers.abstract: We prove that three is the smallest background period for which a one-dimensional discrete Anderson-Bernoulli operator can have infinitely many gaps in its almost-sure spectrum. For an explicit period-three background and coupling, we construct infinitely many bounded gaps accumulating from the right at a spectral energy, for every nondegenerate Bernoulli law. This property persists on an open set of background and coupling parameters. The proof combines a transverse heteroclinic connection and invariant multicones with spectral points from periodic realizations. A strict geometric window permits integer scale matching, and the required parameter inequalities are verified by exact rational arithmetic.

papers.title: Regularity of solutions to complex Monge-Amp\`ere equations in big classes
papers.abstract: We study the non-pluripolar complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation in an arbitrary big class on a compact K\"ahler manifold. Under a weighted Laplacian lower bound on the log density, we obtain local $C^{2,\alpha}$ regularity on the part of the ample locus where the data satisfy the stated hypotheses. A second criterion based on a quasi-plurisubharmonic decomposition gives similar regularity. In particular, a smooth positive density gives a smooth solution on the ample locus. None of these regularity results require nefness of the background class, resolving positively a question of Dinew, Guedj, and Zeriahi.

papers.title: A variational Free Boundary Ricci flow on Surfaces with Boundary
papers.abstract: We study a Ricci flow on a compact surface with boundary arising as the L2-gradient flow of the Liouville functional with its natural Neumann boundary condition. Geometrically, this boundary condition preserves the geodesic-curvature density H d{\sigma}. In the regime in which the total scalar curvature satisfies 0 < C_0 < 4{\pi}, a scale invariant normalised Liouville functional is monotone, and bounded below. In our first result, we use its dissipation to show that every compact blow-up limit is homothetically shrinking with constant positive scalar curvature. We then treat a rotationally symmetric disc with H_0 > 0 and C_0 > 0, in which case every noncompact limit is ruled out via singularity analysis and a noncollapsing theorem. Consequently, the normalised flow fully converges smoothly to the unique spherical cap determined by the initial area and the preserved boundary data, yielding our second result. Additionally, we also study the regime in which C0 is nonpositive. In this case standard PDE arguments prove full smooth convergence of the normalised flow towards a metric with constant nonpositive scalar curvature.

papers.title: Almost minimizing Yang$-$Mills fields: log-epiperimetric inequality, non-concentration, and uniqueness of tangents
papers.abstract: We establish a direct log-epiperimetric inequality for Yang$-$Mills fields in arbitrary dimension and we leverage it to prove uniqueness of tangent cones with isolated singularity for almost energy minimizing connections and $\omega$-ASD connections (where $\omega$ is not necessarily closed) satisfying some suitable regularity and non-concentration assumptions. En route to this we establish a Luckhaus type lemma for connections to exclude curvature concentration along blow-up sequences.

papers.title: Fine properties of nonlinear potentials and a unified perspective on monotonicity formulas
papers.abstract: We rigorously show that a large family of monotone quantities along the weak inverse mean curvature flow is the limit case of the corresponding ones along the level sets of $p$-capacitary potentials. Such monotone quantities include Willmore and Minkowski-type functionals on Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature. In $3$-dimensional manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature, we also recover the monotonicity of the Hawking mass and its nonlinear potential theoretic counterparts. This unified view is built on a refined analysis of $p$-capacitary potentials. We prove that they strongly converge in $W^{1,q}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ as $p\to 1^+$ to the inverse mean curvature flow and their level sets are curvature varifolds. Finally, we also deduce a Gauss-Bonnet-type theorem for level sets of $p$-capacitary potentials.

papers.title: Pohozaev identities and Liouville theorems for $L$-tension energies on manifolds
papers.abstract: We study autonomous energies $B(\phi,e,\|\tau_L\|^2/2)$ for a general Lagrangian $L=L(y,r)$. The scaling derivative $\widehat L=2rL'$ determines the trace of the stress tensor and a vector-field identity on Riemannian domains. For homogeneous $L=a(y)(2r)^{p/2}/p$, the divergence term in this trace vanishes when $p=m$. A conformal vector field with a strictly signed conformal factor then gives $L$-harmonicity for positive mixed tension powers, under explicit integrability and flux conditions. This applies, in particular, to hyperbolic space. On complete gradient Ricci solitons with bounded Ricci curvature, a separate cutoff argument gives a global identity for general $L$. On the cigar and on Euclidean space, direct metric variations give second-order boundary criteria that also cover tension powers $1<q<2$. The applications include target weights and the fourth-power case. Examples distinguish the annular condition from global first-derivative integrability and show why scalar growth bounds or finite tension energy alone do not imply vanishing.

papers.title: Scalar Entropy and Source Terms in Harmonic Ricci Flow on Surfaces
papers.abstract: The modified scalar curvature $S=R-\alpha|\nabla\phi|^2$ satisfies a reaction--diffusion equation with a nonnegative source $Q$ under harmonic Ricci flow on a surface. The relative entropy of $|S|$ need not decrease for either sign of $S$. At a nonzero constant initial value its second time derivative is the spatial variance integral of $Q$, divided by $|S|$. We construct closed examples of both signs with spatially varying tension norm. For $S<0$, normalizing by the mass of $-S$ gives an exact covariance threshold for decay and a sufficient bound in terms of the variances of $\frac{Q}{-S}$ and $-S$, the scalar mass and density bounds, and the first positive eigenvalue. On a torus this variance bound gives decay even when the covariance is strictly negative. For $S>0$ we retain the source and boundary flux in the Hamilton square formula. In the fixed harmonic free-boundary disk case the source vanishes, and equality for a nonconstant map forces $S$ to be constant. The appendices give the boundary terms for the coupled Perelman functionals.

papers.title: Determinants of Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on Constant Curvature Surfaces with Geodesic Polygonal Boundary
papers.abstract: We express the zeta regularized determinants of the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on compact Riemann surfaces with constant curvature metrics and geodesic polygonal boundary in terms of the Laplacian determinant on their closed conical doubles. The formulae apply without restrictions on the genus or number of boundary components. They involve explicit corner angle factors and a quotient of the Reidemeister and $L^2$ norms on the determinant line of cohomology. The proof combines a new relative BFK type gluing formula with the comparison theorem for analytic and combinatorial torsion on manifolds with boundary, due to L\"uck and Vishik. As an application, we give a rigorous proof of the Aurell-Salomonson formula for Euclidean polygons. We also obtain explicit determinants for spherical and hyperbolic triangles and certain other geodesic polygons from known formulae for their doubles and discuss some extremal properties.

papers.title: On $U(1)^{2}$-Invariant Cayley $4$-Folds in $\mathbb{R}^{8}$
papers.abstract: We study $ \mathrm{U}(1)^{2} $-invariant Cayley submanifolds in $ \mathbb{R}^{8} $, under the action with weights $ (e^{i \theta_{1}}, e^{i \theta_{2}}, e^{-i(\theta_{1} + \theta_{2})}, 1) $ on coordinates $ (z_{1}, z_{2}, z_{3}, z_{4}) \in \mathbb{C}^{4} $. Locally, we can prove that $ N $ can be written as a graph of functions $ u, v, a_{1}, a_{2}: \mathbb{R}^{2} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ (where $ a_{3}= -a_{1}-a_{2} $), where unlike in the special Lagrangian setting, the moment-map parameters are not required to be constant, which gives rise to additional degrees of freedom in the reduced equations. We prove that $ N $ is Cayley if and only if a non-linear, Cauchy-Riemann system of partial differential equations in $ u, v, a_{1}, a_{2} $ holds, with ellipticity away from its degeneracy locus. We investigate the special Lagrangian and coassociative reductions of the system, obtaining potential functions in both cases. For general $ \mathrm{U}(1)^{2} $-invariant Cayley $ 4 $-folds, we derive almost-conservation laws (with clear obstruction terms) involving natural $ S_{3} $-invariant and alternating combinations of the moment-map parameters. These identities exhibit additional source terms, distinguishing the general Cayley system from its special Lagrangian and coassociative reductions.

papers.title: Sharp modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality for matrix-valued functions on spheres
papers.abstract: We prove that for every smooth positive definite matrix-valued function $g$ on the unit sphere $S^d$, \[ \int_{S^d}\tr(g(\log g-\log\E g))\dd \le\dfrac1{2d}\int_{S^d}\tr((\Delta g)\log g)\dd. \] Here $\mu$ is normalized area measure, $\E g$ is the spherical mean, and $\Delta$ is the positive spherical Laplacian. This complete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality extends Beckner's sharp logarithmic Sobolev inequality, in its modified form, to matrix-valued functions independent of the matrix size. We show that both entropy and Fisher information decay exponentially under the heat flow with optimal exponent $2d$, whose proof combines the Bochner identity with a $4$th-tensor estimate in the matrix-valued setting.

papers.title: Remarks on thin sets in potential theory for sub-Laplacians
papers.abstract: In contrast to Euclidean cases, we observe that, there are sets in Heisenberg groups that are thin at the origin and block all geodesics from the origin. However, in polarizable Carnot groups, using horizontal radial curves constructed for polar coordinates by Balogh and Tyson, we show that sets, that are thin at the origin, cannot block all horizontal curves. Consequently, we are able to use the asymptotic behavior with respect to the fine topology to estimate the Hausdorff dimension of singularities of potentials for sub-Laplacians and obtain geometric applications.

papers.title: On the Morse index of some Riemannian homogeneous fibrations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we use the technique developed by the first named author in arXiv:2610.07815 to compute the Morse-index of some Riemannian homogeneous fibrations. For the quaternionic (resp. octonionic) Hopf fibration, we compute the index and nullity, where the metric on the $\mathbb{S}^7$ (resp. $\mathbb{S}^{15}$) is the quaternionic (resp. octonionic) Hopf--Berger metric. In particular, for the round metric on the domain, the Morse-index is $45$ (resp. $153$). We also give a spectral formula for the Aloff--Wallach projections. In particular, we obtain that the Konishi $\mathbb{R} P^3$-fibration $N_{1,1}\to\mathbb{C} P^2$ is stable throughout the two-parameter metric family, while the unit tangent sphere bundle $T^1(\mathbb{C} P^2)\to \mathbb{C} P^2$ is stable under some conditions on the metric. We also compute the index and nullity of the Clifford hypersurface in the fiber-squashing range of the quaternionic Berger family. Finally, for the identity map on the quaternionic Hopf--Berger spheres, we determine its Morse--index by an explicit sequence of transition parameters.

papers.title: Uniqueness of tangent flows in mean curvature flow (I): smooth minimal cone
papers.abstract: We prove uniqueness of multiplicity-one minimal-cone tangent flows in mean curvature flow when the cone has a smooth embedded two-sided link and satisfies strict Hardy stability, radial Gaussian nonresonance, and weighted stationary rigidity. We also establish a discrete Lojasiewicz inequality, polynomial convergence rates, and rigidity among smooth self-shrinkers. In particular, these conclusions hold for all Simons cones $\mathcal C_{p,q}$ with $p,q \geq 1, p+q\geq 6$.

papers.title: Algebraic Vector Fields on Compact Homogeneous Spaces are 2-generated
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a compact, connected manifold on which a compact Lie group $K$ acts smoothly and transitively. We show that the Lie algebra of algebraic vector fields on $M$, i.e., of smooth vector fields whose translates under $K$ span finite-dimensional spaces, is generated by two vector fields. Consequently, the subgroup generated by the flows of these two vector fields is dense in the identity component of the diffeomorphism group of $M$. For spheres, explicit generators are obtained from earlier results on spherical vector fields.

papers.title: Equivariant Flow Matching on Homogeneous Spaces
papers.abstract: Flow matching enables the training of networks that can flow samples from an initial to a target distribution. The network is regressed against simple vector fields that are conditioned on end points in the target distribution. In the Euclidean case, these conditional vector fields induce flows along straight lines. Various generalisations have been proposed to perform flow matching on spaces where straight lines are not well-defined, such as Riemannian manifolds and Lie groups. Riemannian flow matching applies to many domains, but typically requires expensive simulation, while flow matching on Lie groups is simulation-free but only works on Lie groups. In this work, we develop equivariant flow matching on homogeneous spaces, which generalises flow matching on Lie groups, while remaining simulation-free. We also derive all generators connecting pairs of position-orientations, generalising, and perform a similar derivation for event-velocity space, the Lorentzian analogue of position-orientation space, so that we can perform flow matching on these spaces.

papers.title: K\"ahler metrics with varying cone angles and Ricci curvature
papers.abstract: We prove that the cone angle of a K\"ahler metric is constant if its Ricci curvature is locally in $L^2$. In particular, a K\"ahler--Einstein metric cannot have a varying cone angle. The proof is elementary and assumes only uniform comparison with the corresponding model.

papers.title: Almost-Global Coordinates on Matrix Manifolds
papers.abstract: We study global coordinates on smooth manifolds outside some closed subsets of measure zero. We first give an elementary proof that every compact smooth manifold admits such coordinates, allowing the Euclidean parameter domain to be disconnected. We then study parametrizations of classical matrix groups, Stiefel manifolds, Grassmannians and real flag manifolds. For these parametrizations, we describe the inverse maps and compute the codimensions of the omitted subsets. We construct these parametrizations using Cayley transforms, graphs of linear maps and block Gaussian elimination. We also give formulas for Riemannian gradients and Haar integrals in these coordinates.

papers.title: Symphonic Joins and Finite-Product Hopf Constructions
papers.abstract: We study how collapse at the ends of a warped product affects symphonic joins and Hopf constructions. For a Hopf construction with a fixed angular map on a finite product of closed Riemannian manifolds, we characterize when the reduced energy has infimum zero among functions connecting the two target poles. Under linear collapse this occurs precisely when, at some end, the collapsing factors have total dimension greater than three, or have total dimension three and vanishing angular density on the collapsing block. In either case the infimum is unattained. For ellipsoidal joins with nonconstant spherical factor maps, smooth extension of a connecting symphonic join forces each factor map to be the restriction of a linear isometric embedding. We also derive the coupled equations for orthogonally split targets, establish a convexity criterion for minimizing separated joins, and construct smooth quaternionic examples with all angular factors active.

papers.title: Rank-sensitive Hodge bounds for symphonic energy and minimizers on sheared tori
papers.abstract: We ask how far the minimum of symphonic energy in a homotopy class can exceed the Hodge lower bound from a pulled-back two-form. For projections from a family of sheared four-tori to the flat two-torus, we compute the minimum and the gap for every smooth shear profile. The gap depends on the variance of the profile. Attainment of the projection's pullback area energy by a coclosed test depends on its oscillation. We determine exactly which variances allow two profiles with the same positive gap and different outcomes for this test, and compute the convex relaxation beyond the oscillation threshold. In arbitrary source dimension the optimized test improves the Hodge bound precisely when the harmonic representative exceeds the rank allowed for the pullback on a set of positive measure. We also prove low-degree cohomology estimates, a sharp universal degree exponent for targets detected by low-degree cup products, and an exact defect identity that forces an immersed source to be symplectic at equality.

papers.title: Pluricanonical locally conformally almost K\"ahler metrics, circle-invariant $G_2$ structures, and Laplacian flows
papers.abstract: We study explicit Hodge evolutions of pluricanonical locally conformally almost K\"ahler metrics and their relation to locally conformal parallel $G_2$ structures. A compact locally conformal parallel $7$-manifold with a parallel non-zero Lee form, carrying a structure-preserving free circle action of constant orbit length orthogonal to the Lee field, has a $6$-dimensional quotient which is pluricanonical with a parallel Lee form and a non-integrable almost complex structure. The fundamental forms upstairs and downstairs are Laplacian eigenforms with an explicit eigenvalue ratio. Conversely, for a fixed normalized $SU(3)$ completion, we characterize the curvature of a circle-invariant locally conformal parallel lift. The lift equations force a pluricanonical base to have parallel Lee form, even locally, and exclude strict integrable pluricanonical bases. Independently, the pluricanonical eigenform identity gives a shrinking solution of He's full Hodge equation and an immortal $d^*d$ solution contracting the Lee plane.

papers.title: Geometry and Stochastic Analysis of Flow and Diffusion Models: A Survey
papers.abstract: Flow-based and diffusion-based models have become the principal means of learning and sampling high-dimensional probability distributions, from images and video to proteins, molecules and physical fields, and increasingly language. Each carries a simple law to the law of the data along a curve of probability measures, and behind the variety of their names lie three geometries, those of the state space on which the data live, of the space of probability measures through which the curve passes, and of the space of paths traced by the generating process. A single analytic idea runs through the subject. Every score identity used to train a diffusion model is an integration by parts, on the noise, on the data or on Wiener space, and Malliavin calculus extends this to nonlinear and infinite-dimensional diffusions. We develop these foundations with full definitions and follow them through normalising flows, flow matching and few-step maps, diffusion models and their convergence theory, conditioning, Schr\"odinger bridges and stochastic control, and their extension to manifolds, Lie groups, discrete and function spaces and jump processes. We close with statistical physics, renormalisation and, more speculatively, holography, in which the radial direction of anti-de Sitter space can play the role of flow time. A table of the main methods and a collection of open problems complete the survey.

papers.title: A singular minimizer of a uniformly convex Hessian-dependent functional
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth, uniformly convex Hessian-dependent energy functional, which admits a singular $C^{1,1}$ minimizer on $\mathbb{R}^5$ that is a two-homogeneous normalization of Cartan's five-dimensional cubic. Our construction relies on constructing a quadratic null Lagrangian for the Hessian that is suitably non-degenerate on the image of the Hessian for the candidate minimizer. This complements a partial regularity result previously obtained by the authors in this setting, and demonstrates that one cannot hope for a fourth-order version of classical second-order elliptic regularity theory \`{a} la De Giorgi-Nash-Moser.

papers.title: Exotic smooth structures on nonorientable 4-manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct closed nonorientable aspherical 4-manifolds with an arbitrarily large number of distinct smooth structures. This uses the reflection trick of Davis-Hayden-Huang-Ruberman-Sunukjian. Our examples become mutually diffeomorphic after either type of stabilization: taking a product with the real line, or taking a connected sum with sufficiently many copies of S^2 x S^2.
